source.title: Looping Beyond Twice: A Scalable Recipe for Looped Mixture-of-Experts
source.authors: Di He; Peng-Xiang Li; Da Chang; Qing-Yan Meng; Lu Yin; Shi-Wei Liu

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some figure and table text is flattened or duplicated by extraction, but the relevant validation-perplexity values are legible.
record.tranche_reason: It tests whether changing recurrent depth at fixed parameter counts changes held-out language-model loss, a different architecture-sensitivity measurement from the original scaling-law studies.
record.gate_note: The paper varies loop count and reports validation perplexity, including under a near-iso-FLOP comparison. It does not fit power laws in parameter count, tokens, or compute, test small-run extrapolation, or derive compute-optimal parameter/token allocations. Downstream accuracies are reported, but the paper does not test their predictability from scale or pretraining loss. References to other scaling-law work are background, not results from this study.
record.test_reason: This is a method paper. It proposes LOOM, a looped-MoE recipe, and reports its validation perplexity against a non-looped baseline, partial-recipe looped baselines and its own ablations. It fits no power laws, extrapolates nothing, and derives no compute-optimal allocation. For V4, looping with shared weights is not a change of conventional shape (depth, width, aspect ratio) at fixed parameters. In the non-iso-FLOP sweeps, per-token compute also grows with loop count, so any loss change is confounded with compute. The partial-recipe blow-ups (†) are training instability, not shape sensitivity. Tables 5 and 6 are component and backprop ablations of the authors' own method. Kaplan and Hoffmann are cited only as background ('scaling axis orthogonal to model size and training data'). The one iso-compute, iso-parameter comparison (Table 2) is a related but different construct and is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude LOOM (residual scaling, embedding re-injection, per-loop routers, Looping Residual, segmented backprop) lets looped MoE scale stably to 9–12 loops; the 1.7B model peaks at 9 loops. Under near-iso-FLOP, 5 loops is best, with 4–6 loops essentially tied. They frame recurrent depth as a compute-efficient scaling axis.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies recurrent loop depth in shared-block MoE language models rather than fitting the original parameter/token/compute scaling laws. It also evaluates a new architecture and training recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Loop count and recipe components matter; outcomes differ between near-iso-FLOP and non-iso-FLOP settings, and segmented versus full backpropagation produces different losses.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed 700M parameters and near-matched per-token FLOPs, trading MoE top-k for recurrent loops lowers validation ppl. It goes from 18.36 to 16.54 (~0.10 nats, ~3.6% of loss), plateauing at 4–6 loops.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At fixed parameters and compute, reallocating compute from active experts to recurrent (weight-shared) depth changes LM loss by a few percent.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed parameters (100M–1.7B), adding loops, and hence per-token compute, with the LOOM recipe lowers ppl with saturation around 9–12 loops (e.g. 1.7B: 9.62→7.77 at 9 loops). Naive looping instead diverges.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Validation loss falls with recurrent compute at fixed parameter count, with diminishing returns, conditional on stabilization.

record.code_released: The text says “Code: LOOM” but gives no URL.
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. The comparisons vary loop count and, in some tables, compute or training procedure; they are not a controlled sweep of width and conventional architecture details. Some table entries are marked as unrecoverable loss spikes.
record.rows_left_out: No validation-perplexity rows from Tables 2–6 were left out. Downstream task accuracies and other metrics are not extracted because this study does not test the version that links downstream performance predictably to parameter/data/compute scale or pretraining loss.

untested.parts: Conventional depth/width/aspect-ratio changes at fixed non-embedding parameters without weight sharing are not studied.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' and V4 'challenges' labels are overturned. V4 concerns shape at fixed parameters in conventional transformers, and roughly fixed compute. Here the rows compare the authors' own weight-shared method with baselines, mostly with compute growing with loops, and the partial-recipe failures are optimization instability. Even the iso-FLOP result (~3.6% loss change) would not clearly contradict 'slight'. No uncertainty is reported; preprint.

versions.untested_parts: No power-law fits in parameters, tokens, or compute.
No extrapolation from small runs to larger runs.
No compute-optimal parameter/token allocation or fitted growth trends.
Tests recurrent loop depth at fixed model parameter count, but not width changes or a broad sweep of conventional architecture details.
Only text language-model pretraining is studied; no other modalities, repeated-data regime, fine-tuning, or transfer.
Reports downstream accuracy across loop counts, but does not test predictability from parameter/data/compute scale or pretraining loss.
Does not compare scaling-law fitting choices, exponents, or compute-optimal splits.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Loop-depth sweeps at fixed model parameter counts, including near-iso-FLOP and non-iso-FLOP settings
reader_labels.reason: Validation perplexity changes substantially with loop depth, improving in LOOM sweeps and sometimes worsening sharply in partial-recipe baselines; this is more than a slight architecture-related effect (rows t2-700m-h2–t2-700m-h6, t3-100m-no-h3–t3-100m-loom-h12, t3-350m-no-h3–t3-350m-loom-h12, t4-17b-h3–t4-17b-h12).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Nine-loop component ablations and segmented versus full backpropagation comparisons
reader_labels.reason: Changing components or training across recurrent depth produces appreciable validation-perplexity differences, including large degradations when components are removed or full backpropagation is used (rows t5-no-res-scale–t5-no-routing-refresh, t6-h3–t6-h12).
